newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / CBOE's VIX dips below 20.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / CBOE's VIX dips below 20.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) volatility index continued sliding on Thursday, dipping below 20 for the first time since late January, traders said.

While recent declines in the stock market's implied volatility levels were widely seen to be a reflection of time-decay concerns ahead of the Easter weekend, some traders said this could be a beginning of a low-volatility period.
VIX, an index of implied volatilities for near-month S&P 100 index .OEX options, slipped to a low of 19.14 in early trade before bouncing back against Wednesday's 20.27 close.

The index had shot up to a high of 25.36 late last week on heightened interest-rate concerns ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Despite a bounce in the OEX this week from the pre-FOMC lows, the volatility shrinkage has significantly dampened gains in OEX calls.

Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer and Co, said Tuesday's Federal Reserve credit tightening had taken out a lot of uncertainty in the market, and he expected a period of low volatility until the market starts to worry about the next FOMC meeting in late May.
"Now that the news is out from the Fed, I would expect it (VIX) to ease off a bit," he said. "As the matter of fact, it broke below its support level."
On the daily chart for VIX, a trendline drawn from recent lows came in in the mid-20 area.
A brokerage trader on the CBOE floor said OEX trading was very slow today, and no one seemed to be willing to pay for the decay during the long weekend.
"Things have just gone quiet ever since the FOMC," he said. Even the most heavily traded April 800 call and 770 put had volume of just over 2,500 lots each by 1100 CST/1700 GMT.
He expected activity to pick up again toward the March employment report due Friday, April 4, but added that jobs data had less importance now than in previous months.
Chris Cadbury of Cadbury Fax Service, an American Stock Exchange member, said the market could stage some surprising up-moves next week as it enters a new quarter.

"There will be new money coming in next week," he said. "The last week of the quarter is very often sloppy, and as a new quarter starts it beomes very different." He said even though volatility tended to be low in a bull market, it made calls more affordable relative to the actual market movement.
"It (low volatility) shows that people don't expect much from the market and that's when big rallies often start," he added.

Cadbury said a number of high downtick readings in the New York Stock Exchange's tick index and relatively high equity put/call ratios in the past few weeks -- even on big up days -- indicated a major bottom had been put in.

He said CBOE equity put/call ratio was at market-basing levels of above 0.50 for nine consecutive days up to Monday, and the ratio on other options exchanges also had positive readings during that period.
